clue.text: Christian joined daughters in lift (9)

indicators.note: D goes into the word for lift

explanation.surface: A Christian convert is said to have joined when daughters were raised up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lift' looks like the elevator a daughter rides; it is the verb hoist, and D is dropped into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a member of the Protestant church founded by John Wesley.

clue.text: Island whisky that’s top of the list? (5)

blocks.note: a malt is a malt whisky
A heads the alphabet and is the top grade

explanation.surface: A whisky from an island that ranks first on the drinks list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top of the list' is not a first letter here (that would give T); it is A, the grade that heads any ranking.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain example: this Mediterranean nation off Sicily is a small archipelago whose main landmass gives it its name.

clue.text: Mark slept naked — something artist might draw with delight (6,4)

clue.text: During day in Rome, lira has no purpose (5)

explanation.walkthrough: The Ides fell mid-month in the Roman calendar (March 15th is the famous one).

clue.text: Accept children disagree (4,5)

blocks.note: issue = offspring, a legal word for children

clue.text: Bold move, Conservative changing old EU pact (4,6)

indicators.note: the letters change their order

explanation.walkthrough: The political surface fits Brexit so well that the French answer hides in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'éclat is a brilliant, striking stroke: a bold move.

clue.text: Chicken half-hearted chef eats cold (4)

to eat is to take something inside, so the chef takes C into its body

explanation.walkthrough: The heart of COOK is OO, so losing half of it leaves COK, and C goes in the gap.

clue.text: Fearless abseiler’s head splits having not tied the knot (6)

explanation.surface: A bold abseiler's head injury comes from a fall, as the knot was never tied.

clue.text: Drunk’s face certainly cheerful — bar adding an hour to time? (8-6)

blocks.note: saving = except, as bar is: 'all saving one'

clue.text: Contract’s approach we really dislike (4,4,4)

explanation.surface: Everyone hates the way this contract was negotiated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a noun, a deal; it is the verb for catching an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Contract here is the verb for catching an illness, and this phrasal verb says the same about flu or a cold.

the shuffled word takes JAC in

clue.text: Record translation of Sino-US conference (10)

clue.text: Criminal needing medical assistance in city, avoiding NY somehow (7)

the letters N and Y, taken out of 'in city'

clue.text: Enjoy Moonstruck very much (4,5)

explanation.surface: A film fan loved the Cher film Moonstruck.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital M makes Moonstruck look like the film title; it is just 'crazy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something like crazy is doing it very much.

clue.text: End producer’s plans (5)

blocks.note: what brings about an end or goal: the method, from the phrase 'to an end'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Producer' is a film word here, but the first half is a cryptic take on 'a means to an end'.

clue.text: Very drunk Irish in A&E showing patience (9)

indicators.note: IR goes in, placed inside A&E between the A and the E

explanation.surface: A very drunk Irishman waits calmly in the emergency department.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is a British hospital's accident and emergency department. Patience is the British name for the card game Americans call solitaire.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire and patience are the same one-player card game.

clue.text: Minister’s office undecorated on tea clipper, say (12)

blocks.note: a clipper is a kind of ship

explanation.surface: A minister's quarters aboard a tea clipper are left bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just sets undecorated after tea. Tea clippers were the fast sailing ships that raced tea home from China.
explanation.definitionFit: By derivation: a chaplain is a minister attached to a college, regiment or hospital, and the suffix -ship names the post.

clue.text: Regular publication of poetry beginning to appear in danger (10)

indicators.note: only the first letter of appear is used
ODIC and A go inside PERIL

explanation.surface: A poetry magazine is in danger of folding.
explanation.walkthrough: ODIC, meaning of an ode, is a word mostly met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a magazine or journal appearing weekly, monthly or quarterly is issued on a regular schedule.

clue.text: Edward made one sandwiches, still needing improvement? (8)

indicators.note: the outer word holds ED like bread round a filling

explanation.surface: Edward makes someone sandwiches, but his cooking could be better.
explanation.walkthrough: Unedited text has not been improved by an editor yet, which is why the definition carries a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: An unedited draft still needs an editor's improvement.

clue.text: Suspect English cat pees, jumping on laps? (14)

indicators.note: the letters are dubious, not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A cat is accused of urinating while leaping onto people's laps.
explanation.walkthrough: Laps suggest a cat on someone's knee; they are circuits of a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeplechasing is racing over jumps, lap after lap.

clue.text: Set off and wandered widely, now distant (9)

indicators.note: SET goes off, out of its order

explanation.surface: Someone who left and roamed the world has drifted away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads as setting out on a journey; split, it is SET made to go off.

clue.text: Sailor’s house given navy telephone (10)

the blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: A sailor's house has a navy-issue phone.

explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Horatio, hero of C. S. Forester's naval novels, rises from midshipman to admiral.

clue.text: The way scarf occupies empty seat in grandstand (8)

clue.text: Tiny chap one can only imagine developing herculean power (10)

definitions.text: Tiny chap one can only imagine

indicators.note: the letters develop into a new form

explanation.surface: A small man can only dream of becoming mighty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the long first half: a leprechaun exists only in the imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: A leprechaun is a tiny imaginary man of Irish folklore.

clue.text: Wearing big top for one purpose (6)

clue.text: 24 hours too long without company (10)

explanation.surface: Spending a whole day alone feels endless.
explanation.walkthrough: '24 hours' looks like a cross-reference to 24 across, but it is just a day, here Friday.

the answer runs through the words

clue.text: Different twins who start to examine who’s the fairest? (4,5)

clue.text: 950 year-old in several books, not one that explains it (4)
